subject: Renewal: Dedicated capacity uplift + autoscale buffer / SLA details
messages:
From: Sam Turner <sam.turner@falkeninc.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Jul 2027 09:15:00 -0700
To: lauren.bishop@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@falkeninc.com
Subject: Renewal discussion — needed GPUs + autoscale guardrails

Hi Lauren,

Our renewal for Dedicated capacity is coming up (ends Sep 15). Usage has been trending up; we expect a 35–50% increase in peak token throughput for the next 12 months. Two asks from our side: 1) reserve an additional 16 GPUs (NVIDIA-A100 equivalent) as part of the renewal commitment, and 2) tighten autoscale behavior — during recent spikes we saw a 90–120s cold-start window that harmed latency-sensitive features.

Concretely, we want to discuss:
- Min / max replica guidance (we were thinking min=6, max=30)
- Warm pool sizing so we have pre-warmed capacity for the most common model variants
- Scale-up lag target (aiming for <=45s to get to requested replica level)
- A throughput guarantee for peak windows (short SLAs for 95th pct latency during scheduled events)

Can we schedule a short call next week? Also, please send any renewal options or draft language you recommend for the amendment.

Thanks,
Sam Turner
Head of Product Ops | Falken Inc.
From: lauren.bishop@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 28 Jul 2027 12:03:00 -0700
To: Sam Turner <sam.turner@falkeninc.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, aditya.rao@redwood.com
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion — needed GPUs + autoscale guardrails

Hi Sam — thanks for the clear asks and for flagging the latency impact.

We can absolutely structure the renewal to reserve the additional 16 GPUs and include autoscale guardrails. Before the call, I wanted to propose two pragmatic paths so we have context for pricing and SLAs:

Option A (Capacity + conservative autoscale)
- Reserved: +16 GPUs (added to your existing Dedicated pool)
- Min replicas: 6; Max replicas: 30
- Warm pool: 10% of max (3 instances pre-warmed for the most-used model family)
- Scale-up lag SLO: best-effort 45–60s; formal 60s SLO for scheduled events (with credits on missed SLOs)
- Throughput guarantee: 95th pct latency target during scheduled events; credits capped at 5% of monthly committed spend

Option B (Higher performance commitment)
- Reserved: +16 GPUs
- Min replicas: 8; Max replicas: 36
- Warm pool: 15% of max (5 instances pre-warmed), plus burst headroom for 10 minutes after schedule start
- Scale-up lag SLO: 45s for scheduled events with a 1.5x credit multiplier on misses
- Throughput guarantee: tighter latency target for 99th pct for defined event windows

I'll loop in Marissa (renewals) and Aditya (technical SLA/product) to validate feasibility and provide a draft amendment. Can you confirm which option is closer to what Falken needs, and whether you have a preferred cadence for scheduled events (weekly batch jobs, monthly campaigns, or ad-hoc)?

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 2 Aug 2027 10:18:00 -07:00
To: lauren.bishop@redwood.com, aditya.rao@redwood.com
Subject: RE: Renewal discussion — needed GPUs + autoscale guardrails

Folks — quick internal take after reviewing usage and current committed spend.

Notes:
- Falken's 30-day peak concurrency aligns with Option A baseline, but their projected growth supports Option B if they want stronger event SLAs.
- Pricing delta between A & B is mostly driven by warm pool sizing and burst headroom. I drafted two line items: one for reserved GPU uplift and one for warm-pool commitment (attached to the outgoing proposal).
- For scale-up lag: our runtime team (Aditya) can commit to a 45s SLO for scheduled events provided we have a warm pool and pre-warming triggers. Non-scheduled ad-hoc spikes remain best-effort with 60–90s typical.

Open questions for Aditya:
1) Can we make pre-warm triggers API-driven (customer calls an endpoint 10–15 minutes before event) or rely on schedule-based pre-warms?
2) For credits: is a capped monthly credit (e.g., 3% of committed spend per missed SLO) reasonable vs. % of event spend?

I attached a short spreadsheet (sla_throughput_table.xlsx) with proposed latency bands and credit tiers. I also put a draft renewal_summary that maps to line items (renewal_capacity_summary.pdf).

-M
Marissa Cole
Senior Renewals Manager | Redwood Inference
From: aditya.rao@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 3 Aug 2027 09:07:00 -07:00
To: marissa.cole@redwood.com, lauren.bishop@redwood.com
Subject: RE: Renewal discussion — needed GPUs + autoscale guardrails

Quick technical confirmation and constraints:

- Warm pool implementation: we can support both schedule-driven pre-warms and an API trigger. API trigger gives Falken more flexibility (call 10–15m out) and avoids over-provisioning.
- Warm pool sizes: pre-warmed instances will be model-family pinned. For their most-used model we can pre-warm up to 6 instances without impacting other customers (this fits Option B warm pool).
- Scale-up lag: 45s to target under scheduled events is achievable when we have warm pool + burst headroom. For ad-hoc spikes, the runtime has an observed scale path of 60–120s depending on model size.
- Monitoring: we will add a per-event trace and token throughput metric to the Redwood Console so Falken can validate.

Recommendation: go to Falken with Option B but include a trial period (90 days) where warm pool sizing is tuned. Offer credits for SLO misses during that trial only (capped). Also include an API-based pre-warm hook in the amendment.

- Aditya Rao
Director, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference
From: lauren.bishop@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 11 Aug 2027 16:42:00 -07:00
To: Sam Turner <sam.turner@falkeninc.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, aditya.rao@redwood.com, procurement@falkeninc.com
Subject: Renewal proposal: Dedicated uplift + autoscale buffer (draft)

Sam — attaching the draft renewal amendment and the SLA table for review. High level: we recommend Option B with a 90-day tuning trial for warm pools. Key bullets (from the amendment):
- Reserved uplift: +16 GPUs added to Falken's Dedicated pool for 12 months (annual renewal).
- Min / Max replicas: min=8, max=36 mapped to your current instance types.
- Warm pool: pre-warm 5 instances for primary model family; API pre-warm endpoint to request additional pre-warms 10–15 minutes before an event.
- Scale-up lag SLO: 45s for scheduled events (defined in section 3.2) for the 90-day trial. Post-trial we will reassess and embed final SLOs in the contract.
- Credits: tiered credit schedule for missed SLOs during trial (capped at 4% of monthly committed spend).

Attachments: renewal_capacity_summary.pdf; sla_throughput_table.xlsx

If this looks good, I can convert to a tracked amendment and send a DocuSign link. Would you like the trial to start on day-one post-signature or aligned to your next big event (you mentioned a Q4 push)?

Thanks — looking forward to closing this out.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0192
